findings.title: The Step 3 gate commands can't separate early exit from counter-gating
findings.description:
Step 3 lists four runs: baseline/counter-gating, early-exit only, subdivision only, and both. But the commands come in identical pairs: lines 162–163 and 166–167 are the same, and so are 170–171 and 174–175. The design adds the `break` unconditionally (lines 36–46) and defines no switch to turn it off. So after implementation, "S=1, counter-gating — should reproduce slice 145 ~38 TPS" (line 161) can't be run.

This leaves two problems:
- A2's "≥5× vs slice 145 baseline" can only be compared against a past 145 number, not re-measured on the same build and host.
- Line 58 says the two interventions "compose multiplicatively", and nothing can confirm that.

Fix one of two ways:
- (a) Add an explicit early-exit flag, threaded the same way as `S`.
- (b) Drop the isolated runs. Say the baseline is the recorded slice 145 measurement, or a run of the slice 145 tag on the same host, and keep only the S=1 and S=3 runs.

Option (b) is lighter and enough to meet A2/A3.

findings.title: `cell_size` and `S` are two independent config fields that can disagree
findings.description:
The component diagram puts both `cell_size (= query_radius / S)` and `subdivision_factor S` on `BenchConfig`. Line 80 says the harness "reads [cell_size] from config", but the doc never says where `cell_size` gets computed from `query_radius` and `S`.

The scan only covers the full query radius when `S × cell_size ≥ query_radius`:
- If a config sets `S=3` but leaves `cell_size=50`, it scans a 7×7 block of large cells. That is correct but slower than baseline.
- If a config sets `cell_size=16.7` with `S=1`, the scan misses neighbors without any error. That breaks the "correct neighborhood is preserved" claim on line 56 and the CLAUDE.md "no silent fallback" rule.

Make `S` the only input and compute `cell_size = query_radius / S` in one place at config load. If both stay configurable, enforce `S * cell_size >= query_radius` next to the existing S validation.

findings.title: S has no defined route into the production engine (slice 146)
findings.description:
S is described only as a `BenchConfig` / bench CLI input (`--subdivision-factor`), with a default of `S=1`. Yet A3's rationale (line 116) is to "confirm headroom exists before slice 146 wires the GPU tick into the production engine". That headroom is measured at `S=3` (line 128). Slice 146 drives `QuadrantsFusedBackend.setup()` from the engine, not from `BenchConfig`. Unless S is a documented `setup()` parameter, the production path runs at S=1 and gets only the early-exit gain.

Line 111 says "Slice 146 is unblocked", but slice 146 needs to know that S, and the derived `cell_size`, are backend setup inputs it must supply. State that in the interface section. Also say whether 149 or 146 owns the production default for S.

findings.title: Some expected-gain figures are wrong
findings.description:
Line 58 says "With S=3 alone: candidates loaded drops to ~5000… With both: candidates loaded ~555". A (2S+1)² scan of cells holding N/S² agents each loads about 49 × 555 ≈ 27,000 candidates at S=3, not ~5,000. The source analysis has the right figure (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:108-111`).

With both interventions, the scan exits after about 32 accepted neighbors, plus however many candidates it rejects before that. The "~555" figure isn't meaningful. The direction of the argument still holds, but fix the figures so no one calibrates A2 or the S choice from them.

findings.title: The S upper bound is justified with wrong reasoning and hard-coded inline
findings.description:
Line 78 says S=8 is "larger than the physical neighborhood". It isn't: by construction, every S gives a scan whose half-width is exactly `query_radius`. It also cites GPU memory risk, but at S=8 on the world size in the 148 notes (756×756), the grid is only about 121² ≈ 15k cells, which is trivial.

The cap is harmless as a sanity limit. However, the literal `8` appears twice in the snippet, and CLAUDE.md requires a value used in conditionals to be defined once as a named constant. Either use a named constant with an honest reason (for example, "beyond this the per-cell loop overhead outweighs the occupancy gain"), or drop the upper bound.

findings.title: The break only exits the per-cell loop
findings.description: The `break` sits inside `for kk`, so once the cap is hit, the agent still visits every remaining `(drow, dcol)` cell, each for one bounds check. At S=3 that is up to 48 cheap iterations, which is acceptable. A one-line statement that this is intended would stop an implementer from "fixing" it with a flag across the nested loops, which adds register pressure (relevant to A5).

findings.title: Line-number references into source code will go stale
findings.description: The doc points to "line 291", "lines 155–184" and "lines 411–462" of `quadrants_fused_kernels.py`. The 148 disposition removes the tiled kernel from that same file (`148-notes.rediagnosis.md:201`), so these offsets will probably shift before implementation. Refer to function or loop names instead, which the doc already gives.

findings.title: The architecture NFR is restated with a specific target
findings.description: The doc restates the Tier 2 NFR (60 TPS at N=50k on CUDA). A3 sets ≥100 TPS with its rationale, matching the slice plan's exit criteria. CUDA-only gates (A2, A3, A5) are kept separate from the checks that can run on a Mac (A1, A4).

findings.title: Scope, dependencies and layering match the slice plan
findings.description:
- The doc declares a dependency only on 145, as the plan entry does.
- It leaves the `TickResult`, world-server, numpy and numba backends unchanged, as the plan's "tick return type contract is the only shared interface" decision requires.
- It keeps the A7 `get_neighbors_first_k` seam (Option A) for the deferred distance-ranked swap, without building that swap now.
- It treats `max_neighbors == 0` as "no cap", matching the project-wide sentinel (`116-slice.knn-spatial-query.md:114`).
- Validation fails at config load with an explicit error rather than a silent clamp.
- The slice adds no new I/O paths or message types, so there are no new failure modes to list.
